items.title: build the test binaries for the six crates
execute.rs canonicalize(): verbatim \\?\ root vs capture-file prefix comparison
items.proves: A figure an engine reports under the canonicalized (on Windows: \\?\C:\...) materialization root is kept by collect_capture_files with a forward-slash relative path (the new probe, a_figure_reported_..., fails on macOS if canonicalize() is removed); a verbatim root works through ProjectContext::discover and the capture upload; the capture_files unit tests build their doc dir from canonicalize() too.
items.does_not_prove: What a real engine (knitr, Jupyter) reports on Windows: knitr/R may print a plain C:\ path or reject a \\?\ path. If a real R run is wanted, render a knitr document by hand with q2 and look for dropped figures.

items.title: positron_cache.rs: vscode_file_uri (drive letter, %3A, non-ASCII) and %APPDATA% rule
items.proves: The URI encoder and the directory rules are internally consistent for Windows inputs (HostOs::Windows is a parameter, so these unit tests ran on macOS too): drive letter lower-cased, colon as %3A, spaces and non-ASCII as upper-case UTF-8 escapes, the %APPDATA% then %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming fallback, normalize_location on all spellings.
items.does_not_prove: That REAL Positron on Windows hashes the same URI (the expected strings come from the same port of uri.ts). Step i2b checks that against a real Positron cache file when you give -PositronDoc.

items.title: real Positron cache file name for a document (optional)
convert_positron_cli: python3 use and literal paths
items.proves: The q2 convert CLI end to end on Windows: exit codes, -o handling, and (only if no caveat is reported) the Python-engine tests that need python3 with ipykernel on PATH. Reading the file found no literal /some/dir path (the old one at line ~113 is gone).
items.does_not_prove: The engine tests are skipped, silently, unless python3.exe with ipykernel is on PATH (a venv has python.exe, not python3.exe; Microsoft Store python3 is a stub). A PASS with a caveat means they skipped: rerun with -WithPython.

items.title: julia_engine_e2e: kill/pgrep cannot run on Windows
items.proves: Both tests that call kill/pgrep return at an `if !cfg!(unix)` guard before any process is started, so nothing is signalled on Windows (PASS means both SKIP lines were printed).
items.does_not_prove: The helpers (kill, pgrep) compile on Windows (b0 proves that) but are never executed here.

items.title: record sources: native-separator display and the capture_driver URI test
items.proves: The record-source list parser, ~ expansion (accepting \ after ~), is-a-directory checks and the diagnostics run on Windows paths; capture_driver builds the cache file URI with the same vscode_file_uri it later matches against, so the import test is self-consistent on Windows.
items.does_not_prove: That the printed path in a diagnostic reads well (inspect one: render with -M "execute.record-sources=C:\nope" and check the message shows C:\nope with native separators), and that the URI equals Positron's (see i2b).

items.title: CRLF: positron-conformance/crlf.qmd and positron-cache/*.ipynb under autocrlf
items.caveat: core.autocrlf is input, not true: the CRLF-checkout case was not exercised. Reclone with: git clone -c core.autocrlf=true ... and rerun -Only i7
items.proves: The conformance, source and knitr-import tests hash the fixtures as checked out (crlf.qmd is a committed-CRLF case; the cache notebooks are LF in git). git core.autocrlf=input; fixtures containing CR bytes in this checkout: crlf.qmd=3
items.does_not_prove: Anything under autocrlf=input/false: with autocrlf unset the LF fixtures stay LF and the checkout is not the stressing case. These fixtures are NOT pinned in .gitattributes (unlike pandoc-recordings), which is why this run matters.
